paper_title: DLP Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
caption: Perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on different validation datasets under varying quantization bits.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The three bar charts, labeled (a) WikiText, (b) PTB, and (c) C4, display the perplexity of the LLaMA1-7B model on different validation datasets as a function of quantization bits, comparing the performance of a "Uniform" quantization method against the proposed "Ours" method. Each chart features a vertical axis labeled "Perplexity" with a linear scale ranging from 0 to 30 for (a) and (c), and from 0 to 400 for (b), with tick marks at regular intervals. The horizontal axis, labeled "Quantization Bits," lists the values 3, 4, 8, and 16, representing the number of bits used for quantization. For each quantization bit value, two bars are shown: a blue bar representing the "Uniform" method and an orange bar representing the "Ours" method. In all three datasets, the perplexity values for the "Uniform" method are consistently higher than those for the "Ours" method across all quantization bit levels. The perplexity for both methods generally decreases as the number of quantization bits increases. The data points for the "Ours" method are consistently lower than those for the "Uniform" method, with the largest difference observed in chart (b) PTB, where the "Ours" method achieves a perplexity of approximately 250 at 3 quantization bits, while the "Uniform" method has a perplexity of approximately 400. In chart (a) WikiText, the "Ours" method achieves a perplexity of about 18.5 at 16 quantization bits, while the "Uniform" method achieves a perplexity of about 26.5. In chart (c) C4, the "Ours" method achieves a perplexity of about 18 at 16 quantization bits, while the "Uniform" method achieves a perplexity of about 24.5. The bars are arranged in a grouped format, with the "Uniform" and "Ours" bars for each quantization bit value placed side-by-side.
model_annotations.English: The bar chart illustrates the perplexity of LLaMA1-7B on three different validation datasets—WikiText, PTB, and C4—under varying quantization bit settings (3, 4, 8, and 16 bits), comparing the performance of a uniform quantization approach (Uniform) against the proposed method (Ours). The vertical axis represents perplexity, with values ranging from 0 to 30 for WikiText and C4, and up to 420 for PTB, while the horizontal axis indicates the number of quantization bits. In all three datasets, the proposed method (Ours) consistently achieves lower perplexity than the Uniform method across all quantization bit levels. For WikiText, the Uniform method shows a perplexity of approximately 29.5 at 3 bits, decreasing to around 26.5 at 16 bits, while the Ours method ranges from about 21.5 to 18.5. In PTB, the Uniform method starts at a high perplexity of approximately 405 at 3 bits and decreases to around 310 at 16 bits, whereas the Ours method starts at about 250 and decreases to roughly 180. For C4, the Uniform method has a perplexity of approximately 29 at 3 bits, decreasing to about 25 at 16 bits, while the Ours method ranges from about 21 to 18. The results indicate that the proposed method maintains lower perplexity across all datasets and quantization levels, suggesting improved performance with less information loss compared to uniform quantization.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm zeigt die Perplexität von LLaMA1-7B auf verschiedenen Validierungsdatensätzen unter unterschiedlichen Quantisierungsbits, wobei die Ergebnisse für drei Datensätze – WikiText, PTB und C4 – in getrennten Balkendiagrammen dargestellt sind. Jedes Diagramm enthält zwei Balkengruppen pro Quantisierungsbit (3, 4, 8 und 16), wobei jeder Balken einer Methode entspricht: „Uniform“ (dunkelblau) und „Ours“ (orange), wie in der Legende angegeben. Die x-Achse repräsentiert die Quantisierungbits und ist in einer numerischen Reihenfolge angeordnet, während die y-Achse die Perplexität anzeigt, mit einem Wertebereich von 0 bis 30 (für WikiText und C4) bzw. bis 400 (für PTB), wobei die Skala linear ist und Tick-Beschriftungen in Abständen von 5 (bis 30) oder 50 (bis 400) angegeben sind. In allen drei Diagrammen sind die Balken pro Quantisierungsbit gruppiert, wobei der dunkelblaue Balken (Uniform) in der Regel höher ist als der orangefarbene Balken (Ours). Die Balken sind in der Reihenfolge der Quantisierungbits sortiert, und es gibt keine visuellen Hervorhebungen wie Schattierungen oder Fettdruck.
